topic: Exploring the Construct of Psychological Safety in Medical Education

sources.title: Exploring the Construct of Psychological Safety in Medical Education
sources.authors: Tsuei SH, Lee D, Ho C, Regehr G, Nimmon L.
sources.journal: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges

findings.finding: Psychological safety allows learners to focus on the task rather than their own image.
findings.quote: Students' sense of PS appeared to free them to focus on learning in the present moment without considering the consequences for their image in the eyes of others.

findings.finding: A lack of judgment from teachers or peers is central to feeling safe while learning.
findings.quote: Students described PS as not feeling judged. Having supportive relationships with peers and mentors improved PS.

principle: Learners engage more effectively with a task when they feel psychologically safe, as this reduces self-consciousness and allows them to focus on the present moment.
for_the_teacher: Explicitly state that mistakes are a normal part of the learning process to reduce the learner's fear of judgment.
Use encouraging language to help the learner focus on the physical sensation of the movement rather than how they look on camera.
Create a supportive environment by acknowledging the learner's progress and effort throughout the session.
